articles.title: Are gender differences really power differences? Large-scale analysis finds strong behavioral parallels
articles.summary: Could the behavioral gap between men and women just be a power gap? New research finds that placing people in powerful roles produces psychological changes that almost perfectly mimic traditional gender differences.

articles.title: Body roundness index linked to depression risk in older adults with dementia
articles.summary: A new study reveals that the body roundness index, a measurement of abdominal fat, is strongly linked to depression in older adults with dementia. The findings suggest this simple screening tool could help doctors identify at-risk patients.

articles.title: A specific thinking style explains why dark personality traits are linked to creativity
articles.summary: Why are traits like narcissism and psychopathy linked to creative success? New research indicates the answer lies in a specific thinking style—one that helps individuals filter out social constraints to focus on novel solutions.

articles.title: Hidden brain wiring may help keep the mind sharp as gray matter shrinks
articles.summary: Scientists have discovered that the brain’s short-range wiring may help protect cognition even as gray matter shrinks with age. Healthier connections just beneath the brain’s surface were linked to better language skills and appeared to weaken the impact of gray matter loss.

articles.title: Scientists find a new layer of Alzheimer’s hidden in the genome
articles.summary: Scientists found that the 3D organization of DNA is disrupted in several types of brain cells affected by Alzheimer’s disease, altering how important genes are switched on and off. The discovery reveals a previously underexplored layer of the disease that could open new paths for understanding and eventually treating Alzheimer’s.

articles.title: Private touch matters more than public affection for relationship quality

articles.title: MDMA-enhanced couples therapy shows promise for treating PTSD and relationship distress
articles.summary: Pairing a brief form of couples therapy with MDMA can lead to large improvements in PTSD symptoms and relationship satisfaction for veterans and their partners, even when only the diagnosed veteran receives the medication.

articles.title: Scientists find Ozempic may slow aging itself
articles.summary: Semaglutide helped older healthy mice live longer while improving memory, muscle function, blood sugar control, and several biological signs of aging. Its effects went beyond those seen with calorie restriction, raising the possibility that GLP-1 drugs could tap into a separate biological pathway linked to longevity.

articles.title: Study of 1.9 million people finds a striking link between ADHD and gut problems
articles.summary: Researchers analyzing data from more than 1.9 million people found that ADHD is associated with substantially higher rates of digestive problems. People with ADHD had nearly double the odds of constipation, 58% higher odds of irritable bowel syndrome, and more than four times the odds of encopresis.

articles.title: Harness or Model? Isolating the Harness Effect in Agentic Coding with a Contamination-Controlled Private Suite
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.11987v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agentic coding system couples a language model to a harness: the tools, prompts and control flow that turn a chat model into an autonomous software engineer. Vendors ship harnesses tuned to their own models, and practitioners assume the vendor-native pairing solves more tasks. We measure that assumption with paired same-model contrasts on a private, contamination-controlled suite of 256 repository and post-cutoff contest tasks. The same 80 tasks ran under claude-agent-sdk and under deepagents on claude-opus-4-8, and under the openai-codex SDK
